topic: Avoiding AI sameness in customer experience
angle: Generative helpers need brand voice, constraints, and an editor—or they erode CX fast.
sourceTitle: The sameness problem behind those unappetizing AI-generated menus
linkedinPost:
Customers can taste “AI sameness.” Sometimes literally.

TechCrunch called out AI‑generated restaurant menus that all read the same—and turn diners off. Swap “menu” for “marketing email,” “support reply,” or “sales proposal” and the lesson holds: unbounded generative tools flatten voice and sap trust.

My take from enterprise rollouts: treat generative AI like a talented junior copywriter. Give it a style guide, a banned list, examples of “do/don’t,” and a human editor. Build constraints into the tool: tone presets, product facts from a source of truth, and personalization that respects customer history.

Track the right CX metrics: conversion and bounce rate lift by segment, complaint volume about “robotic” tone, NPS in cohorts exposed to AI content, and manual-edit rate by team.

If you wouldn’t let a new hire email customers without onboarding, don’t let a model do it either. What guardrails have kept your brand voice intact while still scaling content? #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
